model: DucoBox ventilation units / IQ unit (Modbus RTU, master node)
applies_to: DucoBox Silent Connect, Focus, Energy (all variants) and ECO with the Communication Print option, and the Duco IQ unit (Modbus standard), per information sheet L8000009-B.
summary: Duco residential and light-commercial ventilation systems expose each network component (the DucoBox itself, control valves, sensors, user controls, window ventilators) as a Modbus 'node'. Registers are numbered node x 10 + parameter, with up to ten 16-bit input (read) and ten holding (write) parameters per node. This map lists the DucoBox master node (node 1, registers 10-19): system status, ventilation level and power, plus the system override, auto min/max and action registers.

addressing.note: Duco numbers registers as node number followed by parameter number (node 1 parameter 0 = 10, node 7 parameter 2 = 72). The sheet says its implementation follows the official Modbus specification, so the printed number is the address sent on the wire; masters that subtract one (reading 19 for 20) can be compensated with the RegOffs parameter set to 1.

source.title: Information sheet ModBus RTU
source.pages: p. 1 (settings, functions, offset note), pp. 2-5 (parameter structure, status and action values), p. 6 (DucoBox node table), pp. 7-13 (other components)

notes: Only the DucoBox master node (node 1) is listed because every other component's registers depend on the node number the installer's network assigns. For any component, input and holding register = node x 10 + parameter (parameter 0-9).

Common per-component parameters (from the sheet): input 0 type of module, 1 status, 2 ventilation position %, 9 localisation number; holding 0 target value % (-1 = off), 9 action. Sensor nodes add indoor temperature (°C x 10), CO2 (ppm) or RH (% x 100) in the input block.
Input register Status values differ from the Action values (manual low is 4 in Status but 2 in Action).
Target value (holding 10) is typed INT16 because -1 turns the override off.
The Modbus slave address is set in the display menu or the Duco Network Tool; its default is not stated in this sheet.

registers.name: Status
registers.description: Active ventilation setting of the whole system.

registers.name: Ventilation position
registers.description: Actual ventilation level of the whole system.

registers.name: Localisation number
registers.description: Group number of components that belong together.

registers.name: Target value
registers.description: Overrides the system ventilation level, 0-100 % in steps of 5; -1 = override off (default).

registers.name: Auto min.
registers.description: Minimum level in automatic mode, 0-100 % in steps of 5 (default 10 %).

registers.name: Auto max.
registers.description: Maximum level in automatic mode, 0-100 % in steps of 5 (default 100 %).

registers.name: Action
registers.description: Simulates a user-control press for the zone.

integration.summary: Read input 11-12 for the system status and ventilation level. Control either with holding 10 (target %, -1 to release) or holding 19 (Action, simulates a button press so user controls stay in step).
integration.enable: Fit the Communication Print option (DucoBox) or use the IQ unit's built-in port; set the Modbus address in the display menu or Duco Network Tool.
quirks: Addresses are node x 10 + parameter; read node numbers from the Duco Network Tool.
If the master reads values shifted by one register, set RegOffs = 1 in the Duco display menu.
setup: Default serial settings 9600 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit; change in the display menu.
gotchas: A target value left set overrides the zone and user controls no longer show the true setting; write -1 to release it.

address_note: address = 0-based Modbus wire (PDU) address; documented = as printed in the source.
note: Re-typed from the manufacturer's public documentation (see source) and verified against it. Registers vary by firmware and options; verify against the live device before writing.
